extracted.intended_audience: TIME readers and general pop-culture / SNL fans
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative checklist for assessing the suitability and performance of Saturday Night Live guest hosts, focusing on on-stage skills, how they handle humor/criticism, and the broader impact of their persona on the show and cast. Derived from a TIME listicle profiling 'dubious' hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting and singing ability
rubrics_metrics.description: They can't act or sing — a basic measure of a host's suitability for a sketch/variety show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the headline: hosts who 'can't act or sing' are flagged as poor fits for SNL's sketch and musical segments; deficiencies in these core performance skills are cited as a reason a host is 'dubious.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to take a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: But can they take a joke? — whether the guest star can tolerate being the butt of sketches or criticism without disrupting the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames hosts' ability to handle on-air ribbing as a distinct criterion: a host who cannot 'take a joke' undermines comedic dynamics and can cause problems during the live broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-existing controversy or provocative persona
rubrics_metrics.description: The host's off-stage reputation and controversies that precede their appearance (e.g., 'engendered controversy even before he appeared on air').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIME highlights that some hosts bring controversy into the studio; prior notoriety can affect audience reaction and cast willingness to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offensive content in the host's material (e.g., misogyny)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the host's past routines or public statements contain offensive elements (the page cites 'the misogyny of Clay's stand-up routines').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece uses Clay's misogynistic material as a concrete example of problematic content that can make appearances untenable and provoke backlash from cast or viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on cast dynamics and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the host's presence causes cast members to react (e.g., refusing to perform), thereby affecting the show's functioning ('refused to do the show — effectively ending her SNL tenure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes real consequences—cast members may boycott or leave in protest—so a host's potential to disrupt cast cohesion is treated as a meaningful evaluative factor.
